preflight_text: pec_faces={z_lo} creates an INFINITE PEC boundary AND the geometry contains finite PEC objects. For antennas or finite-GP structures, the pec_faces boundary makes the ground plane cover the entire domain face, which changes the physics (cavity vs radiating antenna). If you need a finite ground plane, remove pec_faces and declare it: a foil is a SHEET (add_thin_conductor, or a zero-thickness PEC Box — one node plane, normal E through it live); a thick plate is a PEC Box VOLUME (walls on both faces, lattice ownership contract #931).

all dielectric(s) ['substrate'] are perfectly lossless in an open (CPML) domain. If you are measuring Q / resonance, this gives an ARTIFICIALLY infinite Q (design-guide Anti-Pattern #1, an R5 surface-metric trap) — add loss, e.g. sigma = 2*pi*f*eps0*eps_r*tan_delta. (Harmless if you are not measuring Q.)

2 conductor sheet dimension(s) are solved more than 1% off their drawn size (worst 2 listed): geometry[1] 'pec' y: drawn 600µm, nodes cover 600µm, solved as 670µm (+11.67%); geometry[2] 'pec' x: drawn 600µm, nodes cover 600µm, solved as 670µm (+11.67%). OBSERVED: the node span the sheet's realized footprint covers on this run's grid, plus 0.35 of the adjacent cell at each free in-plane edge -- a PEC sheet's edge is solved that far beyond its last node (measured on this solver, both polarizations; a flat wall has no such offset). REMEDY: build the in-plane profiles with rfx.mesh_edges.edge_aware_profiles(domain, dx, sheets=[...], solids=[...]) and pass them as Simulation(dx_profile=..., dy_profile=...); a node ON the edge is not the fix. STALE IF: the footprint's node span on the run's node coordinates does not reproduce the printed numbers.

MSL port 'msl_0': only 3 normal interval(s) between the validated ground and trace planes. Validated conductor-plane gap=300.0µm over 3 normal interval(s), from z=0.0µm to 300.0µm (declared height=300.0µm). Separately, the declared-material column has 3 same-permittivity sample slot(s), extent 300.0µm. This material extent is not the conductor-plane gap. The existing resolution recommendation is at least 4 normal intervals and an aligned declared substrate interface. On a uniform mesh, refine to dx ≤ 75.0µm and align the declared ground z=0.0µm and trace z=300.0µm with nodes; on a profiled mesh, place sufficient nodes between those faces. Geometry screening does not quantify Z0 error. The historical sweep and its realized-board Hammerstad-Jensen anchor are pre-#802 records; a new matched-geometry measurement is needed before quoting a current accuracy bound.

UserWarning: compute_msl_s_matrix: reported Z0 for MSL port 'msl_0' = 47.59 ohm deviates 10.9% from analytic Hammerstad-Jensen 53.11 ohm at f = 4.6000 GHz. Z0 rides on the retained N-probe fit (S1 transitional); this can reflect Yee-staircase bias, or that the rasterized board (h_sub/W snapped to the lattice; see sim.fidelity_report()) differs from the declared one — not necessarily an extraction fault (issue #752). Fitted Z0/beta are not used in S11/S21, which use measured V/I and the analytic Z0 anchor; this does not certify those inputs. This port's probe clearance is satisfied, so standing-wave content at the probes is not the cause; refine the mesh or reconcile the rasterized board with the declared one before quoting Z0. Check settling_db, probe_clearance, beta_railed and observation-plane sensitivity before interpreting S.

UserWarning: compute_msl_s_matrix: the returned S is not passive at 103 of 121 frequency bins, worst sigma_max = 1.007 at 3.750 GHz. S is returned exactly as extracted — nothing is clipped, and the per-bin amounts are in sigma_max_excess. A passive structure cannot scatter more power than it receives, so these bins are a measurement artifact rather than physics — the usual causes are a record that ended before the structure rang down and a mesh too coarse for the geometry (see settling_db and reliable for which). Pass enforce_passivity=True to get S projected onto the passive set instead; that projection is skipped on the eps_override channel, so the measured and the differentiated S stay the same function.
